note: Route-graph ratchet baseline (no-new-rot ratchet). Each entry is the CURRENT reachable-first-party-module-count ceiling for a LOCKED FIXED_ROUTES route (the primary dev-perf 'first-party graph pressure' metric from scripts/route-graph.mjs). The gate fails when a tracked route's count grows BEYOND its ceiling and when the committed baseline raises any ceiling vs the base branch WITHOUT a matching absorb record. Counts are captured WITH the companion extension repos cloned pinned (exactly as CI does via clone-extensions) so they reproduce in CI. Regenerate with `node scripts/audit/route-graph-ratchet.mjs --write-baseline` after cloning the extensions — a ceiling should only ever be LOWERED as barrel imports are narrowed, and is never raised SILENTLY. A sanctioned raise must be ANNOTATED: a sibling `absorbs` record `route -> { from, to, reason, pr }` whose from/to exactly match the raise vs the base branch (from = the base ceiling, to = the new committed ceiling, reason = why the growth is accepted, pr = the PR carrying the absorbed change). The gate validates records strictly (malformed/stale/orphan records fail closed; a carried-forward record may not be deleted while its raised ceiling is kept) and prints a LOUD NOTICE line for every absorbed raise. The tracked route set is route-graph.mjs FIXED_ROUTES; change it there, then regenerate.

/api/mcp.reason: cinatra#3026 (epic #3023, lifecycle-c W2) wires the review card's content channel. The review binder hardcoded the content channel's named absence, so the markdown display drew its floor and a floor has no tabs. Reading the pinned revision's text is what the card needs, so the binder imports the projection builder and the text ports as values instead of types. This baseline is the MERGE of origin/main into that branch, so `from` (1756) is main's OWN committed ceiling at 238ba5d1d77470689632992e9995908389672e24, and every carried-forward record for this route is RETIRED BY THIS RAISE, which is the one lifecycle the gate allows for an annotation whose ceiling moves. RE-MEASURED ON THE MERGED TREE, not carried over from the pre-merge baseline: with the companion extension fleet cloned PINNED (116/116, missingCount 0) and the merge's own unmodified scripts/route-graph.mjs, `node scripts/audit/route-graph-ratchet.mjs --write-baseline` on this tree measures /api/mcp 1760, /chat 1863, /api/a2a 1768, /api/llm-bridge 1778 and /sign-in 163. That is main's committed ceiling PLUS AN IDENTICAL +4 on the four routes that reach the artifact renderer dispatch spine, and nothing at all on /sign-in, which does not reach it — so the merge composes main's ceilings with this branch's own +4 and adds nothing of its own. The +4 is the content-channel module with its two value leaves plus the pinned-text module, exactly the growth this branch recorded against main's earlier ceilings before the merge. /sign-in measures 163, 60 UNDER its 223 ceiling, and is LEFT WHERE MAIN COMMITTED IT, record included: a ceiling is a ceiling, and this forward merge does not ratchet an untouched route down. Narrowing is not available inside this change: the edge is not a barrel but the review card's own functional dependency on the content channel, and the binder's only importer sits behind the same dispatch spine these four routes already reach, so moving the import one hop moves no edge. Pushing the read out to the three review route entries as an injected port would remove it from the locked graphs, but that changes a shared exported surface and its call sites, which is a redesign this fix leg does not carry.
